cards.question: What defines an open-container-with-drogue-issues malfunction, and what is its EP sequence?
cards.answer:
Safety pin and main pin are removed from the main closing loop, but the drogue cannot deploy or a collapsed drogue does not extract the main deployment bag. Disconnect RSL; look-grab cutaway handle; arch; peel/pull cutaway; ensure main-riser separation, physically assisting if necessary; look-grab reserve; peel/pull reserve; check deployment; check altimeter.

cards.question: What is the unstable-exit response?
cards.answer:
Attempt to regain stability; set drogue after 10 seconds; if unable to set drogue, Total Malfunction EP.

References: OPS p.59; OPS p.47; IRM p.192

Canopy still in bag: attempt to contain. Biplane: fly front canopy. Side-by-side: gentle inputs, steer canopies into each other. Downplane: cut away main if risers are not entangled. Keep brake settings the same on main and reserve. If landing both, choose large open area and PLF.

cards.question: What is the wire-landing response?
cards.answer:
Disconnect RSL; braked parallel descent to achieve vertical path between wires; prepare to PLF. Upon ground contact immediately cut away and move to safe distance. If suspended, stay until power shut off; avoid touching anyone; do not cut away unless certain you can clear entanglement before reaching ground.

Official-manual comparison [VERIFIED]: The course answer agrees with the cited Sigma procedure.
